title: Forecast horizon scenarios scratchpad — dedicated GPU capacity 1:1
content:
Purpose / context:
- Prep notes for upcoming 1:1 with Mike (platform lead) + quick sync with SRE. Goal: align on Q2/Q3 reservation strategy for Dedicated GPU pools and validate autoscale primitives we should recommend to product teams.

High-level constraints / assumptions (quick mental model):
- Procurement / reservation lead time (hardware + capacity commit) ~ 6-10 weeks from decision to usable pool.
- Committed pool sizing is still the primary lever for predictable per-token cost. Short-lived bursts are okay but expensive if frequent.
- Target utilization bands: cross-team target 45–70% (P50 workload). Anything consistently <40% is wasted; >80% increases queuing risk and latency SLO breaches.
- Baseline traffic growth expectations: product features planned this quarter add ~12–28% more token throughput across hosted customers we plan to serve on Dedicated.

Agenda (1:1):
1) Quick status: current committed GPUs, current avg util (7d / 30d), burst usage stats.
2) Scenario review (conservative / expected / aggressive) + cost delta.
3) Autoscale policy proposal: soft headroom, burst budget, fallback model variants.
4) Procurement cadence & approval thresholds (who signs off at $/mo commit).
5) Action items + owners.

Data snapshot I need before the meeting (ask Ben / Claire to confirm):
- Current pool: 48 A100xT4-equivalent GPUs (how counted: vGPU equivalence note) — demand curve by hour for last 90 days.
- Peak-day concurrency (P95) across teams: 1.8x baseline.
- Token-per-GPU throughput estimate on typical seq=512 mix: ~220k tokens/hour (this is from bench run v4).
- Bursts: average 3 bursts/week >20% above committed capacity, median burst length = 37 minutes.

Scenario sketches (quick numbers, to iterate) — goal: map to commit sizes and burst runway.
1) Conservative (risk-averse):
- Assumes growth +12% and keeps utilization target ~55% P50. Add ~6 GPUs to absorb growth and headroom.
- Commit change: +6 GPUs -> 54 total.
- Expected burst failover: keep same burst policy; +40% budgeting for 2x weekly bursts.
- Rough monthly commit delta: +6 GPUs -> ~$18k/mo (ballpark; confirm pricing).

2) Expected (recommended):
- Growth +20%, target utilization 60%. Add +12 GPUs -> 60 total.
- Enables smoother autoscale (lower queuing), absorbs new features launch with small buffer.
- Provision for scheduled canary windows (2 hours/day) where traffic temporarily duplicates.
- Monthly delta: ~+36k/mo (estimate).

3) Aggressive (growth-optimistic):
- Growth +28–35%, target util 65% with aggressive commit to avoid throttling. +20 GPUs -> 68 total.
- Pros: fewer model fallbacks, consistent latency. Cons: higher committed cost & more risk if ARR doesn't materialize.

Autoscale / routing policy ideas (notes to discuss):
- Soft headroom of 10%: allow autoscale to burst up to +10% of commit from spare dedicated burst pool (fast hot-add), beyond that fall back to cheaper model variants or lower-max tokens.
- Burst budget bucket approach: track per-namespace burst seconds/month and throttle if usage above contract-level. Add alerting when burst runway < 72 hours.
- Fallback ladder: (1) smaller quantized model variant same family -> (2) older checkpoint with degraded quality -> (3) regional reroute to on-demand pool. Implement automatic percentage of traffic to reroute during sustained >5m queue.
- Pre-warm KV cache on scheduled canary windows to avoid cold-start latency in autoscale windows.

Questions I want answered in the 1:1 (open items):
- Mike: what is our appetite for commit spend increases right now (band: low/medium/high)? Any finance guardrails?
- SRE: what's realistic for fast burst capacity hot-add (<10min) — is there infra work or a billing/VM warmup issue we can't solve?
- Sales/Customer Success: are there pending committed-customer deals this quarter that should push us to the aggressive plan? (Claire follow-up)
- Legal/Procurement: any constraints on how we structure reservations vs marketplace credits?

Follow-ups & action items (clear owners + deadlines) — put in my calendar as reminders: 
- Aisha: compile 90-day utilization graphs (P50/P90/P95), include per-team split — due 2026-03-09.
- Ben: run sim for token throughput sensitivity (seq length mix changes +20%/ -20%) and produce GPU-days delta — due 2026-03-11. Linked: JIRA INFRA-4823.
- Claire: confirm two enterprise leads with potential committed usage this quarter and their expected start dates — due 2026-03-10.
- Daniel: feasibility check on hot-add latency and prewarm scripts; prototype automation runbook — due 2026-03-19.
- Mike: sign-off threshold proposal draft (who can approve < $50k/mo vs > $50k/mo) — ask to send comments by 2026-03-12.

Risks / red flags to call out quickly: 
- If bursts are frequent and >1h each, committed pool is the wrong tool (need sticky capacity or rethink routing).
- Billing mismatch: committed discounts might require minimum term; we need to ensure we don't over-commit before product signals are stable.
- Autoscale complexity: introducing many fallback tiers increases testing surface and customer-visible regressions—need canary windows + eval suite.

Quick sketch: simple decision rule for commit change (for discussion) — a checklist:
- 3 signals required to increase commit by +x GPUs:
  1) 30d rolling average util > 62% AND P95 queue time > 250ms for 5+ days OR
  2) Confirmed signed commitments from customers >= 60% of monthly delta capacity OR
  3) Forecasted feature releases that historically add >15% throughput (engineering schedule attached).
If 2/3 true -> approve move to "expected" scenario; if all 3 -> consider "aggressive".

Notes to self: language to use with Mike — frame tradeoff as "latency SLO risk vs committed cost" and propose short-term mitigation (2 months) if we opt for conservative plan: enable tighter fallback + manual on-call scale windows for launches.

Misc quick ideas to preserve runway/capacity efficiency:
- Per-team soft quotas (prevent one team from consuming repeated burst budget).
- Scheduled eviction window for low-priority jobs during peak hours.
- Stimulate better client-side batching by shipping small SDK incentives (co-bill credits for saving tokens)

Meeting prep checklist (what to attach to calendar invite):
- 90-day util graphs (Aisha)
- Burst runbook + logs (Daniel)
- Customer commit list (Claire)
- Sim results skeleton (Ben, if available)

Bottom line (draft recommendation to test in 1:1):
- Recommend "expected" scenario (+12 GPUs) with the following safety nets: burst budget monitoring + automated fallback ladder + procurement sign-off deadline. If Sales confirm >50% of new capacity as committed deals, accelerate to aggressive.

Open TODO (post-1:1):
- Draft short blurb for product teams summarizing policy changes and what to expect if we increase commit (Aisha).
- Create tiny eval harness to measure quality delta for fallback model variants (Claire + Applied ML) — ticket: INFRA-4890 (to create).

Scratchpad thoughts / brain dump (freeform):
- Could we offer teams an internal "burst credit" allocation they can purchase monthly? Might make cost allocation clearer and reduce ad-hoc surge.
- Consider a POC where we autoscale only for specific high-value routes (not entire namespace) to limit cost leakage.
- Keep note: alignment with Redwood Optimize team — their recommendations may change recommended quantization profiles which will shift GPU-day calculations.

End of notes.
